sections.title: Definitions and Interpretation
Employment and Commencement
sections.text:
2. EMPLOYMENT AND COMMENCEMENT

2.1 The Company hereby appoints the Employee as Software Engineer — Backend Systems, and the Employee hereby accepts such appointment, on the terms and conditions set out in this Agreement.

2.2 The employment shall commence on 1 March 2024 (the "Commencement Date").

2.3 The Employee's employment is subject to:
(a) satisfactory completion of reference checks;
(b) verification of academic qualifications;
(c) execution of this Agreement by both parties.

2.4 The Employee confirms that they are not subject to any contractual obligations with a prior employer that would prevent or restrict the performance of duties under this Agreement.

sections.title: Probation Period
sections.text:
3. PROBATION PERIOD

3.1 The Employee's employment shall be subject to a probation period of six (6) months commencing from the Commencement Date (the "Probation Period").

3.2 During the Probation Period, either party may terminate this Agreement by providing seven (7) days' written notice.

3.3 The Company reserves the right to extend the Probation Period by a further three (3) months, subject to written notice to the Employee prior to the expiry of the initial Probation Period.

3.4 Upon satisfactory completion of the Probation Period, the Company shall issue a written confirmation of regularisation.

sections.title: Duties and Responsibilities
Remuneration and Benefits
Working Hours
sections.text:
6. WORKING HOURS

6.1 Standard working hours are 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday to Friday (45 hours per week), with a one-hour unpaid lunch break.

6.2 The Employee may be required to work beyond standard hours as reasonably necessary to fulfil their responsibilities, without additional compensation, as the position is classified as a professional/managerial role.

6.3 The Company operates a hybrid working policy. The Employee is expected to be present at the Company's office in Mumbai for a minimum of three (3) days per week unless otherwise approved in writing.

6.4 Remote working arrangements are subject to the Company's Remote Work Policy, which may be updated from time to time.

sections.title: Leave Entitlements
sections.text:
7. LEAVE ENTITLEMENTS

7.1 Annual Leave: The Employee shall be entitled to 18 days of paid annual leave per calendar year, accruing at 1.5 days per month.

7.2 Sick Leave: The Employee shall be entitled to 8 days of paid sick leave per calendar year.

7.3 Casual Leave: The Employee shall be entitled to 6 days of casual leave per calendar year.

7.4 Public Holidays: The Employee is entitled to all public holidays as notified by the Company each calendar year.

7.5 Leave encashment: Unused annual leave in excess of 6 days may be encashed at the end of the calendar year at the Employee's basic daily rate.

7.6 Leave without pay may be granted at the sole discretion of the Company.

sections.title: Training Cost Recovery
sections.text:
7A. TRAINING COST RECOVERY

7A.1 The Company may, from time to time, invest in the Employee's professional development through external training programmes, certifications, or courses.

7A.2 If the Company bears training costs exceeding ₹50,000 in any rolling twelve-month period, the Employee agrees to the following recovery schedule:
(a) If the Employee resigns within twelve (12) months of completing such training: 100% of the training cost to be recovered;
(b) If the Employee resigns between twelve (12) and twenty-four (24) months of completion: 50% of the training cost to be recovered;
(c) After twenty-four (24) months: No recovery obligation.

7A.3 The aggregate training cost recovery obligation shall not exceed ₹1,00,000 (Rupees One Lakh) in any instance.

7A.4 Recovery shall be effected by deduction from final settlement amounts or by direct payment by the Employee within 30 days of the termination date.

7A.5 The Company shall provide a written training cost statement to the Employee before any recovery is demanded.

sections.title: Notice Period
sections.text:
8. TERMINATION AND NOTICE

8.1 Notice Period: Following the completion of the Probation Period, either party wishing to terminate this Agreement shall provide the other with thirty (30) days' written notice.

8.2 The Company may, at its discretion, elect to make payment in lieu of notice (PILON), equivalent to the Employee's basic salary for the applicable notice period.

8.3 During the notice period, the Employee shall:
(a) continue to discharge their duties diligently;
(b) hand over all pending work and responsibilities to a designated successor;
(c) return all Company property, including equipment, documents, and access credentials.

Non-Solicitation
sections.text:
12. NON-SOLICITATION

12.1 During employment and for a period of twelve (12) months following termination, the Employee shall not:
(a) directly or indirectly solicit, induce, or attempt to solicit any employee, consultant, or contractor of the Company to leave their engagement;
(b) solicit business from any client or customer of the Company with whom the Employee had material contact during the twelve months prior to termination.

12.2 This clause does not prevent the Employee from placing general advertisements for employment not targeted at specific Company personnel.

sections.title: Confidentiality
Intellectual Property
sections.text:
14. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

14.1 All inventions, discoveries, developments, software, designs, processes, and works created by the Employee:
(a) in the course of their employment;
(b) using Company resources, equipment, or information;
(c) related to the Company's business or anticipated business
shall be the sole and exclusive property of the Company.

14.2 The Employee hereby assigns to the Company all such Intellectual Property Rights, both present and future, and agrees to execute any documents necessary to give effect to such assignment.

14.3 The Employee waives all moral rights in such works to the maximum extent permitted by law.

14.4 This clause does not apply to inventions created entirely on the Employee's own time, without Company resources, and unrelated to the Company's business.

sections.title: Data Protection
sections.text:
15. DATA PROTECTION

15.1 The Employee consents to the Company processing their personal data for employment purposes, including:
(a) payroll and HR administration;
(b) performance management;
(c) statutory reporting obligations.

15.2 The Employee shall comply with the Company's Data Protection Policy and all applicable data protection laws.

15.3 The Employee shall not process personal data of clients or colleagues outside the scope of their duties or retain such data after termination.

sections.title: Dispute Resolution
Governing Law
sections.text:
17. GOVERNING LAW

17.1 This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of India.

17.2 Subject to the dispute resolution provisions above, the parties submit to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts located in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

sections.title: General Provisions
sections.text:
18. GENERAL PROVISIONS

18.1 Entire Agreement: This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties relating to the subject matter and supersedes all prior agreements.

18.2 Variation: No variation shall be effective unless in writing and signed by both parties.

18.3 Severability: If any provision is found unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue in full force.

18.4 No Waiver: Failure to enforce any provision shall not constitute a waiver.

18.5 Notices: Notices shall be in writing and delivered personally, by email (with acknowledgement), or by registered post to the last known address of the recipient.

clauses.title: Annual Salary (CTC)
clauses.summary: The employee will receive a gross annual Cost to Company (CTC) of ₹18,00,000, paid monthly at ₹1,50,000.
clauses.plainEnglish: Your total annual compensation package is ₹18 Lakhs per year, paid as ₹1.5 Lakhs every month. This is before tax and other statutory deductions.
clauses.whyItMatters: Your salary sets the financial basis of the employment relationship. Understanding the CTC structure (vs take-home pay) and applicable deductions is important.
whatToVerify: Confirm the exact take-home (in-hand) salary after deductions
Clarify what components are included in CTC vs gross salary
Check whether the bonus is guaranteed or purely discretionary
clauses.originalText: The Employee shall receive a gross annual Cost to Company (CTC) of ₹18,00,000 (Rupees Eighteen Lakhs), payable in equal monthly instalments of ₹1,50,000, subject to applicable tax deductions.

clauses.title: Performance Bonus
clauses.summary: Eligible for up to 15% annual performance bonus, entirely at the Company's discretion.
clauses.plainEnglish: You may receive a bonus of up to 15% of your basic annual salary if you meet or exceed performance targets. However, the Company decides whether and how much bonus is paid — it is not guaranteed.
clauses.whyItMatters: The bonus is discretionary. If you are counting on this income, it is worth clarifying what performance targets are used and how consistently the bonus has been paid historically.
whatToVerify: What specific targets determine bonus eligibility?
Is any portion of the bonus guaranteed?
When in the year is the bonus paid?
What happens to the bonus if you resign mid-year?
clauses.originalText: The Employee shall be eligible for an annual performance bonus of up to 15% of the basic annual salary, subject to the Employee meeting or exceeding performance targets as determined by the Company.

clauses.title: Probation Period
clauses.summary: 6-month probation period, with either party able to terminate on just 7 days' notice. Company may extend by 3 additional months.
clauses.plainEnglish: For the first 6 months, the employment can be ended by either side with just one week's notice. The company can also extend the probation by another 3 months. You receive full notice period protections only after probation ends.
clauses.whyItMatters: During probation, your job security is significantly lower. The short notice period and possibility of extension are important to understand before starting.
whatToVerify: What criteria are used to assess probation performance?
How is feedback provided during probation?
Are salary and benefits the same during probation as after?
Under what circumstances would probation be extended?
clauses.originalText: The Employee's employment shall be subject to a probation period of six (6) months commencing from the Commencement Date. During the Probation Period, either party may terminate this Agreement by providing seven (7) days' written notice.

clauses.title: Notice Period (Post-Probation)
clauses.summary: After probation, either party must provide 30 days' written notice to terminate employment.
clauses.plainEnglish: Once your probation ends, you must give the company at least 30 days' notice if you decide to leave. The company must also give you 30 days' notice if they wish to end your employment (or pay you instead of requiring you to work the notice period).
clauses.whyItMatters: A 30-day notice period means you need to plan at least one month in advance if you intend to resign. This affects your ability to join another employer promptly.
whatToVerify: Does the notice period apply equally to both sides?
Can the notice period be waived by agreement?
What are the consequences of not working the full notice period?
Does the company typically pay in lieu or require the notice to be worked?
clauses.originalText: Following the completion of the Probation Period, either party wishing to terminate this Agreement shall provide the other with thirty (30) days' written notice.

clauses.title: Training Cost Recovery
clauses.summary: If the company spends on training and you resign within 24 months, you may owe back up to ₹1,00,000.
clauses.plainEnglish: If the company pays for your training and you leave within 12 months of completing it, you must repay 100% of the cost. If you leave within 12-24 months, you repay 50%. The maximum you can owe is ₹1,00,000. The money is deducted from your final paycheck or you must pay within 30 days.
clauses.whyItMatters: This clause creates a financial obligation that can make it expensive to leave the company after receiving training. The ₹1,00,000 cap provides some protection, but this is still a significant financial commitment.
whatToVerify: Which specific training programmes trigger this clause?
Must the company disclose the training cost before you agree to participate?
What happens if the company initiates your termination — do you still owe the recovery?
Is ₹1,00,000 the absolute cap or just an example?
clauses.originalText: The aggregate training cost recovery obligation shall not exceed ₹1,00,000 (Rupees One Lakh) in any instance.

clauses.title: Confidentiality Obligation
clauses.summary: Confidentiality obligations continue for 2 years after employment ends.
clauses.plainEnglish: You must keep company information secret both during and for 2 years after your employment. This covers technical data, client lists, business plans, and financial information. Disclosing this information without permission could expose you to legal action.
clauses.whyItMatters: Post-employment confidentiality obligations can restrict what you can discuss with future employers or colleagues. The 2-year period is significant and survives termination by either side.
whatToVerify: Is the definition of 'Confidential Information' broad enough to affect your next role?
Are there any carve-outs for publicly available information?
What happens if you inadvertently disclose information?
Does this obligation apply if the company terminates you?
clauses.originalText: Post-employment: These confidentiality obligations shall survive termination and shall remain in force for a period of two (2) years following the date of termination.

clauses.title: Intellectual Property Ownership
clauses.summary: All work created during employment — or using company resources — belongs to the company.
clauses.plainEnglish: Anything you build, write, or invent during your job belongs to the company. This includes software, designs, and processes created using company time or resources. There is a narrow exception for work done entirely on your own time, using your own resources, unrelated to the company's business.
clauses.whyItMatters: If you have side projects, open-source contributions, or personal creative work, this clause could potentially cover them if they overlap with the company's business area or are created on company time.
whatToVerify: What counts as 'company resources'?
Does working from home on personal equipment change the analysis?
Should you disclose existing side projects before signing?
How does this interact with prior inventions you own?
clauses.originalText: All inventions, discoveries, developments, software, designs, processes, and works created by the Employee in the course of their employment, using Company resources, equipment, or information, or related to the Company's business or anticipated business shall be the sole and exclusive property of the Company.

clauses.title: Non-Solicitation
clauses.summary: For 12 months after leaving, you cannot approach company employees or clients for business.
clauses.plainEnglish: For one year after your employment ends, you cannot try to hire away the company's employees or consultants, and you cannot try to take the company's clients. This applies regardless of whether you resigned or were terminated.
clauses.whyItMatters: If you are planning to start a business or join a competitor after leaving, this restriction could affect your ability to bring colleagues or clients with you for 12 months.
whatToVerify: Does this apply even if the company terminates your employment?
How is 'material contact' with clients defined?
Does a general job advertisement count as solicitation?
What consequences are stated for breach?
clauses.originalText: During employment and for a period of twelve (12) months following termination, the Employee shall not directly or indirectly solicit, induce, or attempt to solicit any employee, consultant, or contractor of the Company to leave their engagement.

clauses.title: Dispute Resolution (Arbitration)
clauses.summary: Disputes must first go to negotiation, then mediation, then binding arbitration in Mumbai.
clauses.plainEnglish: If you have a disagreement with the company, you first try to sort it out directly (30 days). If that fails, you go to mediation. If mediation fails, the dispute goes to a private arbitration process in Mumbai — not a regular court. The arbitrator's decision is binding.
clauses.whyItMatters: Arbitration is typically faster and more private than court litigation, but it may limit your access to certain remedies available in regular courts. Understanding the process matters before a dispute arises.
whatToVerify: Who bears the cost of arbitration?
Can you still go to court for urgent matters?
Are there any employment law claims excluded from arbitration?
clauses.originalText: If not resolved within 30 days, the parties shall submit the dispute to mediation under the rules of the Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration (MCIA). If mediation fails, the dispute shall be referred to binding arbitration.

clauses.title: Annual Leave Entitlement
clauses.summary: 18 days paid annual leave per year, plus 8 sick days and 6 casual leave days.
clauses.plainEnglish: You get 18 paid vacation days each year, 8 paid sick days, and 6 casual days. Leave builds up at 1.5 days per month. Unused vacation over 6 days can be converted to cash at year-end.
clauses.whyItMatters: Understanding your leave entitlements helps you plan time off. The ability to encash unused leave is a useful financial benefit.
whatToVerify: Must leave be approved in advance and is approval guaranteed?
What is the process for carrying forward unused leave?
Are the 6 casual days for any purpose, or is documentation required?
clauses.originalText: The Employee shall be entitled to 18 days of paid annual leave per calendar year, accruing at 1.5 days per month.

clauses.title: Termination for Cause (Immediate)
clauses.summary: The company can terminate immediately without notice for gross misconduct, fraud, or serious breach.
clauses.plainEnglish: In certain serious situations — such as fraud, misconduct, or a major breach of the contract — the company can end your employment immediately without any notice period or payment in lieu. This is sometimes called 'summary dismissal'.
clauses.whyItMatters: Understanding what constitutes grounds for immediate termination helps you understand the limits of acceptable conduct and the protections available to you.
whatToVerify: How is 'gross misconduct' defined in the Company's disciplinary policy?
What process must the company follow before dismissing for cause?
What appeals mechanisms are available?
clauses.originalText: The Company may terminate this Agreement immediately without notice or payment in lieu of notice in the event of: gross misconduct; serious breach of any term of this Agreement; conviction of a criminal offence; fraudulent or dishonest conduct.

clauses.title: Data Protection
clauses.summary: Employee must comply with data protection laws and the company's data policy.
clauses.plainEnglish: The company will process your personal data for HR purposes. You must also follow data protection rules when handling client or colleague information, and cannot take that data with you when you leave.
clauses.whyItMatters: Handling personal data outside company policies can expose both you and the company to legal liability under applicable data protection laws.
whatToVerify: What data does the company collect and how long does it retain it?
Who has access to your employment records?
clauses.originalText: The Employee shall comply with the Company's Data Protection Policy and all applicable data protection laws.
